summary: Port reproduces the same easing-curve demo — identical curve sequence, cadence, hue mapping and marker motion — but draws the curve half as thick (whole render ~45% dimmer), uses a white marker instead of red, and in the overshoot/undershoot easings it lets the curve fall off the grid instead of clipping it to the edge, leaving 6-8 of 16 columns blank.
observations: Rig is a 16x16 grid (default). Both sides draw the same three elements: a gray y=x reference diagonal, a rainbow curve y=ease(x) whose hue equals the eased value (0=red at value 0, sweeping the full wheel to red again at value 1), and a single marker pixel on row 8 that ping-pongs left-right.

Both sides step to a new easing curve every ~5 s; the curve is static within a mode and only the marker moves. Motion-stat peaks at 20 fps: orig at 4.95, 9.95, 14.95 ... (exactly 100 frames = 5.00 s apart); port at 5.00, 10.05, 15.10 ... (101 frames = 5.05 s apart). At 5 fps: orig every 25 frames (5.0 s), port every 26 frames (5.2 s). The port holds each easing exactly one frame too long, so the two slowly slip out of step (a full easing apart after ~100 modes at 20 fps, ~26 modes at 5 fps).

Easing SEQUENCE matches mode-for-mode. Column-by-column curve profiles were compared at mid-mode for modes 0-35 (t=2.5 ... 177.5 s) and 36-51 (t=182.5 ... 257.5 s, each side sampled at its own mid-mode time to cancel the drift): mean absolute row difference ~0.25-0.44 px in every normal mode, i.e. the same curve family, order and strength on both sides for 52 consecutive modes. Neither side had repeated its library by 260 s.

Stroke thickness: the original plots each column as a 2-3 px tall run (e.g. mode 0 at t=2.0 s, column 3 lit at rows 0 AND 1), the port plots exactly 1 px per column. Summed over 36 sampled mid-mode frames the port lights 658 curve pixels against the original's 1301 (ratio 0.51). Mean brightness over a 60 s window: orig 20, port 12.
Reference diagonal: original draws it at RGB 76,76,76; port at 30,30,30 — ~2.5x dimmer, so the linear reference is much fainter against the curve.

Marker colour differs: original's marker is pure red (255,0,0), port's is white (255,255,255). Marker POSITION and timing are identical — dumped at 0.2 s steps over 4 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps, both sides sit on row 8 at the same columns (0, 1-2, 3-4, 7, 11-12, 14, 9, 5, 2, 0 ...) on the same 2.0 s ping-pong cycle, and that period is fps-invariant on both sides (2.0 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps), so the marker easing is time-based and matched.

Overshoot/undershoot easings are where the port breaks. In modes 21-23 (t~105-120 s) the original clamps values outside 0..1 to the edge row and draws a solid 2-3 px bar along the top or bottom of the grid, keeping all 16 columns lit (39, 38, 36 lit pixels); the port drops those samples off-grid entirely and lights only 10, 10 and 8 columns (11, 11, 10 pixels). At t=106.5 s the original shows a thick band across rows 0-2 for columns 0-10 plus a rising tail; the port shows columns 0,1,2 at row 0, columns 3-8 completely dark, then the tail. Same failure at t=113 s (original: solid red bar across row 14 from column 5 to 15; port: isolated dots at columns 5, 6 and a 3-px bar at 13-15) and again at mode 51 (t=260 s, columns 3-8 blank). Visually those windows turn the port from a continuous rainbow ribbon into scattered dots.
Both sides expose ZERO controls (probe run: 'no settable controls' on orig and port), so the control surfaces match.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both). Output is fully deterministic: seed 1234 renders byte-for-byte the same stats as seed 1 on both sides, so the pattern ignores the RNG.
Steady state is healthy on both: brightnessTrend 'steady' on both over 6 s, 60 s and 240 s windows; no decay, no freeze, no runtime or compile errors on either side.
feedback: Draw the curve with the original's stroke weight. The original lights 2-3 pixels per column (the sample lands between two rows and both are lit); the port lights exactly 1. That single change accounts for the whole brightness gap — orig mean brightness 20 vs port 12 over 60 s, 1301 vs 658 lit curve pixels across 36 sampled frames.

Clamp the plotted curve value to the visible range instead of discarding off-grid samples. In the easings that undershoot below 0 or overshoot above 1 (modes 21-23 at t~105-120 s, and mode 51 at t~260 s) the original pins those samples to row 0 / row 15 and draws a continuous bar along the edge; the port drops them, leaving 6-8 of 16 columns completely unlit. Check against t=106.5 s (original: rows 0-2 filled for columns 0-10; port: columns 3-8 blank) and t=113 s (original: solid bar across row 14, columns 5-15; port: two dots plus a 3-px stub).
Recolour the marker pixel on row 8 from white (255,255,255) to pure red (255,0,0) — position and 2.0 s ping-pong timing are already exact, only the colour is wrong.
Brighten the gray y=x reference diagonal from 30,30,30 to 76,76,76.

Shorten each easing's dwell by one frame: the original changes curve every 100 frames at 20 fps / 25 frames at 5 fps (exactly 5.00 s), the port takes 101 / 26 frames (5.05 s / 5.2 s). The extra frame looks like an accumulator being reset to zero after the threshold rather than having 5 s subtracted from it.

Everything else is already right and should not be touched: the order and shape of the easing library (verified matching for 52 consecutive modes, out to 260 s), the hue = eased-value colour mapping (per-column RGB identical), the 2 s marker ping-pong, and the empty control surface.
